import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 951

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
 - [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ.,
    New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
-/

open scoped Finsupp Nat.Prime Topology
open Filter

namespace Erdos951

/-- A sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` is said to have property `Erdos951Prop` if for any pair of distinct
finitely supported sequences `k l : ℕ →₀ ℕ` their corresponding Beurling integers are of distance
at least one apart. -/
def Erdos951Prop (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k ℓ : ℕ →₀ ℕ), k ≠ ℓ → |beurlingInteger a k - beurlingInteger a ℓ| ≥ 1

/-- If a strictly increasing sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` has property `Erdos951Prop`
and `1 < a 0`, then `a` is a sequence of Beurling prime numbers. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : 1 < a 0)
    (hm : StrictMono a) (he : Erdos951Prop a) :
    IsBeurlingPrimes a := by
  refine ⟨ha, hm, tendsto_atTop_atTop.2 fun x => ?_⟩
  by_contra h_contra
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) :=
    ⟨_, tendsto_atTop_isLUB hm.monotone (isLUB_ciSup ⟨x, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun n =>
    le_of_not_ge fun hn => h_contra ⟨n, fun m hm' => hn.trans (hm.monotone hm')⟩⟩)⟩
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Metric.tendsto_atTop.mp hL (1 / 2) (by norm_num)
  have := hm (by linarith : N < N + 1)
  have h_diff : a (N + 1) - a N ≥ 1 := by
    rw [← abs_of_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ a _ - _)]
    simpa using he (.single (N + 1) 1) (.single N 1) (by simpa [Finsupp.ext_iff] using ⟨N, by simp⟩)
  linarith [abs_lt.1 (hN N le_rfl), abs_lt.1 (hN (N + 1) (by grind))]

/-- If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a →
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊ := by
  sorry

/-- Beurling conjectured that if `1 < a 0 < a 1 < ⋯` has property `Erdos951Prop` and the number
of reals in $[1, x]$ of the form $\prod_i a_i^{k_i}$ is $x + o(\log x)$, then `a` must be the
sequence of primes. Property `Erdos951Prop` makes distinct exponent vectors give distinct
Beurling integers, so counting the set `BeurlingIntegers a` counts the generalised integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a → Erdos951Prop a →
    ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos951

findings.description: The variant assumes `Erdos951Prop a`, requiring all distinct exponent-vector products to be at least 1 apart. In Er80, p.103, Beurling's conjecture is introduced for a general increasing sequence with counting function x + o(log x); unit separation is introduced only in the following paragraph, for Shapiro's question. Lean therefore appears to state only the separated special case of Beurling's conjecture. Separation is stronger than the injectivity needed to identify counting values with counting representations. I classify this as questionable because the narrative in the directly cited Er77c and on the problem page could instead be read as carrying the preceding separation assumption into the Beurling remark; I did not establish an equivalence reduction that settles this scope ambiguity.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory” (1980), p.103, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf: “The following nice conjecture is due to Beurling. Let 1 < P₁ < ⋯ be a sequence of real numbers … Assume that B(x) … = x + o(log x). Then the P's are the primes.” Only subsequently: “In this connection H.N. Shapiro asked … Assume that the numbers … differ by at least one.” This paper is linked by the cited https://www.erdosproblems.com/951. Hilberdink–Lapidus, arXiv:math/0410270, §1.1, explicitly count generalized integers with multiplicities.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether this declaration intentionally states only the separated special case. To state the general Beurling conjecture from Er80, remove `Erdos951Prop a` and count representations using `({k : ℕ →₀ ℕ | beurlingInteger a k ≤ x}.ncard : ℝ)` instead of the cardinality of the range. Retain `IsBeurlingPrimes a`; it ensures bounded representation sets are finite. If the separated special case is intended, identify it as such and supply a reference supporting its solved status.

reformulations.difference: For the source's sufficiently-large-x interpretation, Lean counts indices rather than sequence values and uses the natural-valued prime-counting function at the natural floor of a real argument.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Strict monotonicity makes the map from qualifying indices to sequence values bijective. The hypotheses imply divergence, so every sublevel set is finite. For every prime p, `(p : ℝ) ≤ x` iff `p ≤ ⌊x⌋₊`, including negative x because primes are positive. Finally, eventual truth at real `atTop` is equivalent to a sequence-dependent threshold X followed by truth for every x ≥ X. The complete equivalence with that value-counting, real-prime-counting formulation was proved in scratch Lean.

could_not_verify: Erdos951.erdos_951.variants.beurling — whether the cited Beurling remark intentionally inherits unit separation, or denotes the general formulation explicitly presented in Er80; see the questionable scope finding. Its recorded solved status was also not independently verified.
review.notes: The website explicitly distinguishes the all-x and sufficiently-large-x readings and reports a counterexample only to the former; Lean's eventual formulation is therefore not a defect. Scratch Lean proofs established finiteness of both counted sets, injectivity of the product map under separation, equality of value and representation counts under separation, equivalence of Iic and Icc 1 counting, and an ordinary-prime model satisfying the hypotheses. Empty products and small prime-counting inputs were checked. No status contradiction was established: the main OPEN tag matches the website, but the consulted sources do not supply a resolution reference for the Beurling variant's `research solved` tag. The reviewed file was not changed.
